commits.message:
fix(strip): the notch lead is U+E0D7, not U+E0D6

U+E0D6 is Nerd Fonts ple-right_hard_divider_inverse: beside a coloured cell it
draws a left-pointing hole, an arrow pointing out of the run. The notch the
ticket describes, and the name it cites (ple-left_hard_divider_inverse), is
U+E0D7: an empty triangle based on the cell's left edge, pointing into the run.
Outlines read from JetBrainsMonoNerdFont-Regular.ttf with fontTools.

docs/strip.md and the POWERLINE_JOINER_GLYPHS comment describe the shape
correctly and say the lead is a Powerline Extra glyph that classic
powerline-patched fonts lack; the join() table no longer describes the lead
as reaching back.

chore(release)!: 0.17.0

The default powerline lead changed shape, which is breaking for 0.x.

feat(strip)!: the default powerline lead is a notch cut into the first cell

POWERLINE_JOINER_GLYPHS leads with U+E0D6 (inverse right-arrow) instead of
U+E0B2. Drawn by the existing cap painter (fg = the cell's background, no bg),
it inks the top-left and bottom-left of the cell and leaves a right-pointing
triangle empty, so a coloured run opens notched, as if an arrow before it
pointed in. The notch is the terminal's own background showing through, so it
matches under a translucent terminal background; a reverse-video U+E0B0 notch
drew visibly darker there. The arrow, divider and tail are unchanged.

BREAKING CHANGE: new PowerlineJoiner() draws U+E0D6 as its lead cap, not U+E0B2.
Pass { ...POWERLINE_JOINER_GLYPHS, lead: "" } for the old shape.

fix(render)!: colour depth governs SGR only — hyperlinks are their own fact (#159)

* fix(render)!: colour depth governs SGR only — hyperlinks are their own fact

segmentsToString/segmentToString take a required `hyperlinks` argument;
renderToString gains a `hyperlinks` option (default true). A null colour
system (NO_COLOR, colour depth none) no longer strips OSC 8 links. Console
and Live emit links exactly when the destination is a terminal, so piped
output stays plain.

* chore: 0.17.0

* fix(render): one resolver decides colour depth and hyperlinks together

resolveDestination(spec, detect) → { colorSystem, hyperlinks } replaces the
three copies of spec resolution in Console, Screen and renderToString.
An explicit depth keeps links (a file sink at truecolor keeps them again);
under auto, links follow the terminal probe without NO_COLOR, so TERM=dumb
and non-TTY output stay linkless while NO_COLOR keeps them.

* fix(color): FORCE_COLOR is a preference too; Console takes a hyperlinks option

FORCE_COLOR=0 no longer drops links on a terminal; forced-on FORCE_COLOR
still keeps them on a pipe. ConsoleOptions.hyperlinks mirrors renderToString's
so a file sink can ask for plain text. resolveColorSystem gets its JSDoc back.
